caption: The drawing features a rectangular woven textile sample set against a plain light beige background. The textile is composed of a plaid pattern made up of intersecting bands in dark blue, red, and yellow, with some smaller areas of cream or off-white. The design alternates between large dark blue squares and bright red squares, both bordered by yellow-green lines creating a grid structure. The left side and lower edge of the textile show a clean, squared edge, while the right edge and part of the lower edge are unfinished, with numerous colored threads (blue, yellow, and red) extending outward in a fringe-like manner. The density and structure of the plaid pattern vary slightly towards the right, becoming more compressed and intricate, while the left side displays larger, more even squares. The entire composition is oriented horizontally and centered, with the textile sample occupying most of the image space and leaving a broad margin of empty background around it.
title: Handwoven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
